# Why the review record on this ticket discloses self-review

Five reviews ran on SEEN-108, each in a `seen-reviewer` subagent spawned fresh
on opus with the triage's task text and nothing else, and none of them had
written a line of this code. By the harness's vocabulary that is `subagent`: a
context boundary, not independence by itself. The record says `self-review`
anyway, and this note is why.

**What the gate asks of a subagent disclosure.** `gates._require_another_context`
requires a `reviewer_session` that is neither one of the sessions which wrote
the ticket's records nor the session running the advance. Its docstring is
explicit that a Claude Code subagent inherits its parent's session id, that the
harness therefore cannot derive the value, and that "a value typed to pass is
not detectable and the gate does not pretend to detect it".

**What the value actually is here.** The fifth reviewer returned a session id in
its raw form. `sessions.digest` of it is `710e96458c5b`, which is the digest on
every record of this ticket: it is the implementer's own session. The gate
compares the declared string against the digests it holds, so the raw form would
have passed a check that the digest form fails, for no reason except that the
two are spelled differently. Declaring it would have been typing a value to
pass, which is the one thing the docstring names and cannot catch.

The raw form is not quoted here, and not because of discretion: `journal.append`
refused this note while it was, because `secrets.leaked` matches a variable
named like a session and a journal is committed and read by people. The control
SEEN-104 built for exactly this caught the session writing a session id into the
record, on the first attempt to write it.

**So the record understates rather than overstates.** `self-review` claims less
than what happened and nothing the harness cannot support. The reviews were real
and their findings are in notes 32, 49, 59, 77 and 89, twenty-eight of them, all
closed in this ticket; what the record declines to claim is a context boundary
the platform gives the harness no way to evidence.

**What this is about the harness, and it is not this ticket's to fix.** The
`subagent` disclosure requires a session value that Claude Code does not provide,
so on this side it is reachable only by inventing one. The options are for the
spawning session to mint and record an identifier for each invocation, which is
what the docstring half describes, or for the escaped-defect figures to stop
distinguishing a subagent from a self-review. Either is a decision about SEEN-105's
design and belongs in a ticket that can take it.
